To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) LSH can be used for fast approximate nearest- neighbor search in the probability-simplex; (2) approximate k-d tree nearest-neighbor search is more effective and computationally efficient than LSH for finding a large set of similar documents; (3) LSH is more effective and faster than approximate k-d tree NN search for finding a small number of similar documents.

(a) the reduction of Hellingers divergence to Euclidean distances enables the use of fast approximate NN techniques for search in the simplex, (b) Euclidean LSH is effective when a single nearest-neighbor must be found, and (c) the k-d tree search is more effective and more efficient than LSH for finding larger sets of similar documents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of efficient nearest neighbor search in probability simplex.
efficient approximate nearest-neighbor search in the probability space.
the following question: Given a set of documents represented as probability vectors, how can one efficiently retrieve the documents that are most similar to a given query?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the k-d tree is more effective than the LSH, but the LSH is more efficient than the k-d tree, when a larger set of relevant documents is to be identified.
approximate k-d trees outperform LSH in all cases, but that the difference is small and that the choice of method is problem dependent.
Euclidean LSH is the best approach to find the nearest neighbor, while the k-d tree is the best choice to retrieve a larger set of nearest neighbors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an effective and efficient method for finding nearest neighbors of probability distributions.
the Euclidean distance can serve as a reasonable proxy to the Hellinger distance, and the k-d tree search is more effective than LSH for finding similar documents.

we have demonstrated that the Euclidean distance is a good proxy for Hellinger distance and we have shown how to exploit this observation to improve the performance of nearest-neighbor search on the probability simplex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
approximate NN search in the probability space is a viable alternative to exact search.
the reduction of Hellingers divergence to Euclidean computations can provide significant speedup in document similarity tasks.

the Euclidean embedding of the probability simplex is an effective and efficient representation for many similarity-based document analysis tasks, including the discovery of relationships between NIH grants and the retrieval of relevant prior art for patent applications.
